name: wv
desc: Programs for accessing Microsoft Word documents
why: Old tools for pulling text out of binary Word .doc files, a classic dive into an undocumented binary format.

brief.what_it_is: wv is a set of programs and a library for reading Microsoft Word binary .doc files. It parses Word 2000, 97, 95 and 6 formats, with some support for Word 2 files, which are converted to plain text. The library is meant for other programs to use, and the bundled command-line tools (wvHtml, wvLatex, wvDVI, wvPS, wvPDF, wvText, wvRTF, wvAbw, wvWml, wvSummary and others) turn a Word document into HTML, LaTeX, DVI, PostScript, PDF, plain text, RTF, AbiWord format, WML, or metadata. wvSummary prints metadata from Office documents.
brief.why_it_exists: The project was started as mswordview and renamed wv because the old name was too close to Microsoft's product WordView. The homepage frames it as a way to give other programs access to Word documents so they can convert them to other formats; it is currently AbiWord's Word importer and informs KWord's importer.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internal mechanism beyond saying the library loads and parses the binary Word formats. Each helper script is a convenience wrapper around the power-user wvWare application, which has many command-line options. The README gives no further detail on the parsing approach.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the 1.2.0 release switched dependencies to libgsf (instead of libole2), libxml2 (instead of Expat) and glib (instead of libiconv), so the build needs those. Windows requires the GnuWin32 port. wvDVI requires latex, wvPS requires dvips, and wvText gives textually correct output only if lynx is installed. wvMime is meant to be plugged into a browser or mail client as a MIME helper and shows the document in GhostView, with intermediate files in /tmp. No accounts or first-run configuration are mentioned.
brief.standout: The project openly deprecates nearly all of its own command-line utilities, saying they should be replaced by AbiWord, while keeping the library itself and wvSummary alive. The homepage is also candid that the framework cannot support features like tables of contents and that bug reports for the tools are no longer accepted.
brief.status: quiet. The newest dated item is version 1.2.1, a minor bugfix release from March 2006, preceded by 1.2.0 in October 2005. The page does not mention a later release, and the maintainer note says the project is hosted on SourceForge and bugs are tracked on the AbiWord Bugzilla. No commit dates were visible.
brief.caveats: Most of the utilities are deprecated, and the maintainers are not accepting bug reports or feature requests for them. The README says wvWare's output has lower fidelity than AbiWord's, and some features such as TOCs are impossible in its framework. wvText output is poor without lynx. wv is licensed under the GPL. Platform support claims include most Unix-likes, OS/2, AIX, OSF1, AmigaOS and VMS, with varying success, and Windows depends on the GnuWin32 port. The brew caveats field was empty.
quotes: wv is a library which allows access to Microsoft Word files.
Warning: all of the utilities (with the exception of wvSummary) should be considered deprecated in favor of using AbiWord.
wvSummary prints out metadata from your Microsoft Office documents. Not deprecated; actually useful.
